page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Venation — definition
lines: The arrangement of veins and veinlets in the
lamina of a leaf is called venation.
steps.why: The definition needs both words - veins AND veinlets - and the place, the lamina (leaf blade).
common_mistakes: Writing only 'arrangement of veins'. Veinlets are part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Veins + veinlets in the lamina - three v-l words in one line.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with veins, veinlets and lamina in it.

steps.label: Dicot vs monocot
lines: Monocots: parallel venation - the veins run
parallel to one another. Ex: Musa (banana).
steps.why: One contrast pair with one example each: net-like in dicots, parallel in monocots.
common_mistakes: Swapping the examples - Hibiscus is the dicot, Musa the monocot.
steps.memory_tip: Monocot leaves such as banana show straight parallel lines; dicot leaves show a net.
steps.margin_note: Both terms with one example each - four short items in all.
